# Form

Form state and validation wired to the fields.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Validation shared by every product team.

- **Use it when:** Any form that checks answers and shows errors next to the fields.
- **Not when:** A single control that saves at once (a switch).

Instead:

- [Field](./field.md): How one control is laid out.

## How Multi-brand uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An error message</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> color.status.danger and a sentence</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> The brand color</div></div><div class="cap">Status colors are shared, never branded.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">The words of an error</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Shared across brands: plain and specific</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Brand tone in errors</div></div><div class="cap">Errors read the same in every brand, so support can help anyone. Example: “Your card was declined. Try another card or contact your bank.”</div></div></div>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] Errors are announced, linked to their fields, and the first one gets focus on submit. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add form
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Form reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.

### Read straight from the system

Form has no variables of its own yet; it reads these system tokens directly.
